title: W4: team tasks, actions, reports and a delivery outbox, kept on files or PostgreSQL and delivered by a job
request: Build W4 of the approved collaborative workspace plan: persist the W1 tasks, actions and reports and deliver them reliably, following the memory bases storage pattern, with a team_delivery job kind, bounded retry, deduplicated replies and a restart requeue.
spec: dclab_rnd/teamspace/store.py (FileTeamWork: one work.json per project under its lock; PgTeamWork: team_task, team_action, team_report, team_delivery in migration 0026, ids unique within a project), dclab_rnd/teamspace/delivery.py (one team_delivery job per task delivering its rows oldest first: recheck the initiating member with write permission, a pluggable target under a time limit, mark delivered; a failure ends the job with the attempt and next time on the row; the relay requeue_undelivered at worker start and on every recovery tick), the TeamWork Protocol in dclab_rnd/storage, and tests on files and PostgreSQL.
plan: read the W4 plan, the owner's delivery rules and the W1 contracts and tests
read the memory bases store, the job store, worker and handlers, and revalidate_job_scope
add the four tables to models.py and migration 0026
write one set of rules over a transaction that files and PostgreSQL both implement
write the delivery job, its settle step and the worker's start-up requeue
write the owner's examples as tests and run them on files and on PostgreSQL
fix the ten findings of the independent review, each with a test, and rerun on files and PostgreSQL

decisions.decision: The outbox rows are the handoff history: a task, a clarification, its answer and a reply each travel as one delivery row
decisions.why: what travels between teams is exactly what the history shows, so one ordered table gives both the delivery state and the owner's numbered lines without a fifth table

decisions.decision: The rules are written once against a small transaction interface; files hold one document replaced whole under the folder lock, PostgreSQL one transaction under a per-project advisory lock
decisions.why: a task and its delivery must be saved together on both stores, and one implementation of the rules cannot drift between them

decisions.decision: A child task is made only through delegate with its stored siblings; a status change only through validate_transition with its stored children and their joined reports
decisions.why: the budget check and the parent's completion check are only true when they read every sibling and child from the store, not what a caller passes

decisions.decision: One terminal record per action, and one succeeded or simulated record per retry key (also a partial unique index on PostgreSQL); a failed attempt followed by a success under the same key is allowed
decisions.why: W1 defines the retry key as what makes a retried attempt the same side effect; refusing every second terminal record would forbid retrying a timeout, which the owner's plan asks for

decisions.decision: Captured as team.handoff events with what set to task.created, task.delivered, action.finished, report.stored and delivery blocked or refused, not new kinds
decisions.why: a new kind moves the experience contract to v18, which needs regenerated schemas, a baseline, the adapter's KINDS_MISSING and a changelog entry, all outside this package's files; team.handoff already carries thread, team, from, to, what and state as meta

decisions.decision: The default delivery target only acknowledges the row
decisions.why: W5 supplies the agents; until then the row itself is the recipient's inbox and the store's reads show it

decisions.decision: One delivery job per task, delivering that task's pending rows in their saved order, stopping at a row whose next attempt is not due
decisions.why: a corrected reply (r2) must never reach the thread before the reply it corrects (r1); keying the job by row let r2 overtake r1 in backoff

decisions.decision: A failure ends the job and records the attempt and its next time on the row; the worker's recovery tick runs the relay, which queues every task whose next row is due
decisions.why: a sleeping backoff held a worker thread and was lost when the worker stopped; the row is the durable state, so any worker can pick it up

decisions.decision: Ids are unique within a project on both stores, and the file store keeps one document per project under that project's lock
decisions.why: the PostgreSQL lock was per project while the file lock covered the whole workspace; per-project files match it, and the keys follow so files and PostgreSQL agree on what an id means

decisions.decision: store_report and supersede_report take the problem's current brief revision as a required argument
decisions.why: the problem brief's revision is not problem memory's base revision (that one starts at 0 and moves on every fact edit), so the caller that owns the brief must name it rather than the store guessing

decisions.decision: The delivery job is queued as the member of the task's oldest pending row, and every row is rechecked with write permission
decisions.why: with sign-in on the worker rechecks the job's user, and a member made a viewer must not have work delivered in their name

change: dclab_rnd/teamspace/__init__.py, store.py, delivery.py (new); dclab_rnd/storage/migrations/versions/0026_team_work.py (new); dclab_rnd/storage/models.py (team_task, team_action, team_report, team_delivery); dclab_rnd/storage/__init__.py (TeamWork Protocol, open_team_work); dclab_rnd/jobs/handlers.py (team_delivery kind); dclab_rnd/jobs/worker.py (requeue_deliveries at start and on each recovery tick); tests/test_teamspace_store.py and tests/test_teamspace_delivery.py (new).

findings.defect: With sign-in on, a revoked member's delivery job failed inside the worker before the handler ran, and the outbox row stayed pending forever.
findings.scenario: Omar starts a task, loses his membership, and the worker's own revalidation raises AccessDenied: the job fails, the row is never refused and the requester never sees why.
findings.cause: the worker rechecks the job's user before calling the handler, so the handler's refusal path never runs
findings.fix: the kind's settle step rechecks the member from the row and refuses it with the reason

findings.defect: A child task made by an agent had no initiating member, so its delivery skipped the member recheck.
findings.scenario: Data Science's agent delegates the ETA question with no signed-in person; the child's delivery row carried initiator None and would be delivered even after Sara lost access.
findings.cause: the initiator was read only from the current principal
findings.fix: a child takes the parent's recorded initiator when no member is given

findings.defect: The first migration declared every primary key twice, on the columns and in a PrimaryKeyConstraint.
findings.scenario: Alembic would build a table with a duplicated primary key definition or fail on upgrade.
findings.cause: the column helper kept primary_key=True while the table also named its constraint
findings.fix: primary keys only through named PrimaryKeyConstraint entries
findings.test: tests/test_storage_postgres.py test_the_migrations_produce_exactly_the_modelled_schema and the downgrade round trip

findings.defect: A target may be called twice for the same row when its worker dies after the target acted and before the row was marked delivered.
findings.scenario: W5's agent posts a reply, the process is killed, the restart requeues the row and the agent is called again for it.
findings.cause: delivery is at least once at the target; only the row's own posted mark is exactly once
findings.fix: documented: the row id is the idempotency key every target must honour; W5 must dedupe on it
findings.test: none yet: W5's targets need a test that a second call with the same row id posts nothing

findings.defect: The capture reuses team.handoff, which 28.2's board hand-offs also write, so a reader counting team.handoff mixes the two.
findings.scenario: store coverage and journeys that read team.handoff for the orchestra board will also see task.created and report.stored.
findings.cause: a new kind needs an experience v18 with schemas, baseline, adapter and changelog changes outside this package
findings.fix: the what field names each event; a v18 with team.task_created, team.delivered, team.action_finished and team.report_stored is proposed

findings.defect: The outbox had no relay: a row stayed pending with no job after a failed authority check, a worker stopping during backoff, or a failing store write.
findings.scenario: The accounts database blips during the check; the job fails, settle swallows it, and the row waits for the next restart.
findings.cause: requeue ran only at start, and settle ran before the dying job ended so its enqueue hit ActiveJob
findings.fix: the relay runs on every recovery tick; a failed job counts an attempt through delivery_failed so the limit holds

findings.defect: The reason the requester sees carried raw exception text, a password and a customer e-mail in the probe.
findings.scenario: A database error from the target became 'Not delivered ... a password ... and a customer e-mail' on the requester's page.
findings.cause: the reason was built from str(exc)
findings.fix: the reason is fixed words plus the error's class; the text is kept only in last_error, credentials removed and passed through dclab_core.redact; AccessDenied gets fixed words too

findings.defect: The history showed refused and undelivered rows as if they had travelled.
findings.scenario: Omar's question, refused at delivery, appeared as '2. Business → Data Science · Omar's question'.
findings.cause: the history read every row regardless of state
findings.fix: refused rows are left out, each entry carries its state, and history_lines marks the others '· not delivered: <state>'

findings.defect: A newer row of a task could be delivered before an older one.
findings.scenario: r1 waits in backoff, r2 corrects it and is delivered first; r1 then lands last and the thread ends on the superseded answer.
findings.cause: one job per row, each delivered independently
findings.fix: one job per task delivering its rows oldest first, stopping at a row not yet due

findings.defect: The migration did not tell the next migration where the chain stands.
findings.scenario: A parallel session numbering its migration after 0024 would branch the history.
findings.fix: 0026 keeps down_revision 0024 and says the next migration uses down_revision '0026' (W2's 0027 does)

findings.defect: Authority at delivery accepted a read-only member, and a task could name a problem its project does not have.
findings.scenario: A member demoted to viewer still had their queued request delivered; a task carried another project's problem id.
findings.cause: revalidate_job_scope was called without require_write, and create_task never resolved the problem
findings.fix: require_write=True at delivery; create_task resolves the problem in its project (resolve_problem) and refuses otherwise

findings.defect: Delivery text was cut to 2,000 characters before it was saved.
findings.scenario: A long clarification lost its end in the row itself, against the owner's rule never to cut before saving.
findings.cause: the row builder sliced the text
findings.fix: the row keeps the whole text and the receipt; only the history cuts what it shows

findings.defect: The file store locked the whole workspace while PostgreSQL locked one project, and one file grew with every project.
findings.scenario: Two projects' writers waited on each other on files and not on PostgreSQL; five thousand tasks made each write rewrite megabytes.
findings.fix: teamspace/<project>/work.json under that project's lock; ids unique within a project on both stores

findings.defect: Backoff slept inside the worker thread, and a hung target held the worker forever.
findings.scenario: Five attempts with doubling waits held a worker slot for half a minute; a target that never returns blocked it for good.
findings.cause: the retry loop waited in the job, and the target was called inline
findings.fix: a failure ends the job with next_attempt_at on the row (the relay requeues it when due); the target runs under a time limit and a timeout counts as a failure

findings.defect: Four smaller faults: accept_reply got the parent's own brief revision, a retried create_task with a new time was refused, a withdrawn clarification was saved as an answer, and move recorded no event.
findings.scenario: A child reply on an outdated brief joined its parent; a request retried a second later failed; cancelling while waiting for Sara sent her note to Data Science.
findings.cause: the brief revision defaulted to the parent's, task identity compared every field, the answer branch did not check the new status, move had no capture
findings.fix: current_brief_revision is required, identity fields decide a retry, only a move back to accepted carries an answer, and move emits task.moved

measurements.name: teamspace store and delivery tests on files and on PostgreSQL
measurements.gate: both test files pass on files and with --pg with no skipped test, and test_storage_postgres, test_jobs and test_storage_interface still pass on both
measurements.result: store 27 and delivery 18 tests a run (file and PostgreSQL classes each), 0 skipped, with and without --pg; test_storage_postgres 4, test_jobs 18, test_storage_interface 6 pass on files and PostgreSQL
measurements.next: W5: the deterministic agents as delivery targets, deduplicating on the row id
limits: no live model is involved; the recipient is scripted
make check-quick and make check-all were not run in this package
the relay runs on the recovery tick (half the stale time, capped), so a retry may wait longer than its backoff
a target cut off by the time limit keeps running on its own thread and may still act; targets must dedupe on the row id

outcome: Tasks, actions, reports and their deliveries are kept on files (one document per project) or PostgreSQL through W1's rules, delivered once per row and in order per task by a team_delivery job that rechecks the member with write permission, never waits in the worker, and is picked up by the relay at start and on every recovery tick; the ten review findings are fixed with tests; no agent consumes them yet.
lessons: Read the worker's own checks before writing a handler's refusal path: a check that runs first can make the handler's branch unreachable.
An outbox row that keeps what travelled doubles as the handoff history, so the history cannot disagree with delivery.
Make the durable row the only state of a retry: a wait inside a job is lost when the job is, a time on the row is not.
risks: The experience capture shares team.handoff with the orchestra board until a v18 kind is added.
Targets must be idempotent on the row id; W5 has to prove it.
Ids are unique within a project, not across a workspace: a caller that looks a task up by id alone must name its project.
